comment:
As someone who has closely observed Karachi’s retail industry, I found this discussion insightful but, frankly, incomplete. While Dolmen Mall undoubtedly deserves the praise for its role in Khaadi’s growth, it’s surprising that Park Towers wasn’t even mentioned by name.

From my perspective, Park Towers was a cornerstone in shaping Karachi’s retail landscape and played a vital role in the early success of numerous brands, Khaadi being one of the most prominent. It provided a critical platform for emerging businesses to establish themselves and connect with a growing, diverse customer base. Brands like Junaid Jamshed, Ego, Sapphire, Outfitters, Bonanza, Scentsation, GulAhmed, Maria B, and my own Heritage Jewellers owe much of their initial success to the visibility and foot traffic Park Towers provided.

While Dolmen Mall is certainly noteworthy and has contributed greatly to the retail evolution, the importance of Park Towers in the success stories of Khaadi and many other brands cannot and should not be overlooked. Its contribution to the retail history of Karachi is undeniable, and it deserves the recognition it has long earned.

title: Stock Watch Special: Unwrapping the Khaadi IPO | Ft. Khaadi Executive Director | Nukta Business
description:
Is the Khaadi IPO a golden investment opportunity in Pakistan’s fashion retail sector, or do complex corporate structures and sponsor payouts raise major red flags for minority investors?

On today’s special episode of Stock Watch, Nukta’s Moiz Ur Rehman and Shahbaz Ashraf, CFA, are joined by Kashif Shah, Executive Director at Khaadi Pakistan, to break down the merits, demerits, valuation metrics, and structural concerns surrounding Pakistan's premier retail listing on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX).

Together, they take an in-depth look at Khaadi Pakistan Limited’s draft prospectus ahead of its public offering, unpacking critical questions surrounding the use of IPO proceeds for bridge loan repayments, recent 1.6 billion dividend payouts, related-party transactions with Texmarks and Weaves Properties, the PKR 8 billion Brand Usage Right (BUR) valuation, pre-IPO investor discounts, and the underlying unit economics of Khaadi's expansion into new Experience Stores.

What do you think about Khaadi’s IPO strategy and valuation? Drop your thoughts in the comments below!
